knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A tradition-based claim needs a named source and a stated link to the class. Naming the music or the price does not establish authenticity.
Unclear mixing of sources can cost trust with both groups of clients. The Australian legality of a class is not the point of this lesson, and nothing in the lesson makes a class unlawful.

A lineage claim is a factual claim about training and needs a record of who trained the teacher and what was taught. Certificates alone do not establish a lineage, and follower numbers are irrelevant.

practicalCriteria: Candidate writes one brand sentence that names the primary source and the intended client group. The assessor confirms the sentence matches the candidate's real training.
Candidate produces a claim list with an evidence reference for every claim. The assessor checks at least three references against the held records.
Candidate completes a side-by-side review of website, timetable and bio text, and identifies at least one inconsistency and the correction made.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Brand sentence saved with its date
Claim list with an evidence reference for each claim
Assessor sign-off on the practical criteria
stopWorkCriteria: A public claim about lineage, certification or results is about to be published and the business cannot evidence it
A health or treatment claim is about to be published before it has been checked
A named teacher or lineage is attributed to the business without a training record or the teacher's consent
